title: Project Overview
description: The README is the stock create-vite Svelte template, so it mostly confirms the stack (Svelte 5, TypeScript, Vite) rather than documenting the calculator itself. Use it to set context, then treat AGENTS.md and package.json as the real sources of truth for what this project actually does: a Voxel Blade damage calculator and build optimizer. This tour then walks from the boot sequence down through game data, the calculation engine, state, and finally the UI and deployment.

title: Application Entry
description: index.html is the browser entry: it loads /src/main.ts into the #app container. main.ts injects Vercel analytics and mounts App.svelte, the root component that orchestrates every build editor and damage panel. Following this two-hop chain first shows that the whole app is a single component tree hanging off App.svelte, which everything in later steps slots into.

title: Core Types & Domain Model
description: src/lib/types.ts is the most imported file in the codebase (21 incoming edges): every data module, engine module and store leans on the StatMap, weapon part types and BuildState it defines. dmgTypes.ts layers the computed damage interfaces (ComputedHit, PerkOnHitDmg) plus the badge config the results UI renders. Understand these types first and everything downstream reads like plugging values into a well-specified contract.
languageLesson: TypeScript: types.ts models the game domain with a StatMap keyed by StatKey plus weapon/blade/handle/glove/essence part types, while dmgTypes.ts adds the computed damage contracts (ComputedHit, PerkOnHitDmg). Reading the key unions and shape of these records is the fastest way to understand what the rest of the codebase is computing.

title: Game Data Modules
description: The src/data directory holds the raw game knowledge: weapon arts, per-perk damage formulas, buff/debuff catalogs and stat-boost handlers, backed by the JSON item registries (perks.json, blades.json, etc.). weaponArts.ts and Perkbasedmg.ts are the two biggest catalogs, while BuffData.ts assembles the active buff list and statboost.ts applies perk-driven stat mutations in a fixed order. These are pure data plus lookup helpers: the engine imports them, but they never touch the DOM or the store.

title: Engine Pipeline
description: engine/build.ts is the hub of the whole calculator (17 outgoing edges): calcBuild accumulates stats from every equipment slot, finalizes perks, then deriveResults computes CDR, boosts, crit, buffs, weapon results and the damage-type distribution. It delegates to weapon.ts (blade/handle merging, weapon-type resolution), enchant.ts (stat selectors, upgrades, infusion) and shrine.ts, all re-exported through the engine.ts barrel. Following calcBuild is effectively following the damage pipeline from BuildState to BuildResult.

title: Constants & Utilities
description: Two thin but vital layers sit under the engine. constants.ts (and constants/index.ts) aggregate the tuning values for perks, boosts, damage types, CDR and draconic mechanics, while utils.ts provides roundMultiplier, calcProcChance and warding multipliers that keep every number consistent. Like types.ts, these are low-level and shared everywhere, so they appear near the root of the dependency graph.

title: Build Store & State
description: store.ts holds the single source of truth for the current build as Svelte writable/derived stores. Its derived result store runs calcBuild live so every UI change recomputes damage instantly, and mutation actions (setEnchantment, setGuild, moveArmorSlot) keep the build valid while debounced writes persist to localStorage. Every editor from step 9 reads and writes through this one store, which is what keeps the whole UI in sync.
languageLesson: Svelte: store.ts uses the classic writable/derived store pattern (with $ store subscriptions in components) rather than Svelte 5 runes. The derived result store re-runs calcBuild whenever the build writable changes — the same reactive mental model as $derived, but through the older store API.

title: Damage Calculator UI
description: DamageAnalyzer.svelte is the main analyze screen (~7.5k lines): it runs the full damage pipeline over the build store and renders per-hit breakdowns, while BaseDamageCalc.svelte turns computed hits into per-type damage rows with crit, lifesteal and DoT colors. DmgTotalTooltip.svelte adds the animated per-type pie chart. This is where the engine's BuildResult becomes the numbers you actually see.

title: Build Editor Panels
description: The rest of the UI is a set of focused editor panels mounted by App.svelte: LevelBar handles level and HP fill (recomputing effective max HP), EmotionalTracker writes the emotional state, BuffList shows and toggles the active buff/debuff list derived from equipped items, and CdrStepsCalc renders cooldown reduction as a chain of multiplication steps. Each one binds to the build store from step 7, so they all stay in sync automatically.

title: Modals & Search UI
description: Selecting any equipment part opens a modal built on the shared Modal.svelte shell (with focus trapping) and ModalSearchHeader.svelte (search, filters, sort). EnchantSelect.svelte is a full accessible combobox with keyboard navigation, and SuggestDrop.svelte renders type-ahead suggestions with the text highlighting helpers from utils.ts. Together they form a reusable selection system that keeps App.svelte from turning into one giant file.

title: Build Saves & Persistence
description: BuildSaves.svelte implements save/load/export/import into localStorage slots with a search index, confirmation modals and toast feedback. Its storage keys, default-build shape and compressed encode/decode maps live in constants/storage.ts, and store.ts's debounced autosave uses the same contract. This is the persistence layer that makes a build survive a page reload.

title: Configuration
description: package.json lists the toolchain (Svelte 5, Vite, TypeScript, Vitest, fallow, Playwright, PWA) and the scripts you will run day to day (dev, build, check, test). vite.config.ts sets the base path, Svelte plugin, PWA service worker and bundle visualizer, while tsconfig.json extends tsconfig.app.json so svelte-check validates app code. Together they define how source becomes the deployed static site.

title: CI/CD & Deployment
description: Deployment is a simple static-site story. The GitHub Actions workflow (static.yml) checks out the repo, installs dependencies, runs the build, and publishes ./dist to GitHub Pages on push, while vercel.json serves the same dist output on Vercel with immutable asset caching. Both depend on the npm build script from package.json, so a working local build is all CI needs.
languageLesson: GitHub Actions: static.yml is a YAML workflow — the on: push filter defines when it triggers, jobs declare a runner, and steps chain actions like actions/checkout with run: shell steps, then actions/deploy-pages publishes the build artifact.

title: Tests
description: The test suite lives in tests/ and exercises the pure engine modules. piercer.test.ts covers getWeaponConditionalBoost multipliers per weapon type and hit scope, Piercer's true-damage conversion behavior, and cross-type damage-boost leak prevention. Because the engine is pure functions over the types.ts data model, this kind of data-driven math is easy to verify without a browser.
